messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran an overnight long-context interleaved regtest (chat + embeddings + slot rotation). Observed sustained KV memory growth; looks like slots are being allocated faster than compaction reclaims them.
kevin: Numbers? rough delta and which counters are moving?
maria: from kvmem snapshot: kv_total_slots=720k; active_slots 460k -> 610k over 8h; fragmented_pages_pct from 9% -> 54%; compaction_invocations=0 for entire run. Heap delta ~+2.6GB.
josh: can you share the exact command and trace id so I can pull the full flame?
maria: repro: ./tools/kvstage --suite interleave-rotate --iters 150000 --seq-dist bimodal --trace 2275008990

Perf snippet:
```
kv_total_slots: 720000
active_slots: 460000 -> 610000
fragmented_pages_pct: 9.1 -> 54.2
compaction_invocations: 0
avg_kv_reuse_latency_ms: 0.7 -> 2.2
top_alloc_sites: kv_store::page_alloc (42%), kv_cache::slot_meta (29%), kv_cache::fragment_map (18%)
```

toni: we relaxed the eviction watermarks in 3.7.2 to shave p99. sounds like this workload (rapid alternation of short/long contexts) prevents free runs long enough for compaction to trigger.
alex: small fragments never coalescing would do this. Do we log free-run length histograms anywhere?
maria: not in baseline run. Starting an A/B: (A) 3.7.2 current watermarks, (B) 3.6 watermarks + KV_OPPORTUNISTIC_COMPACT=1. Kicking off now.
devops-bot: queued job kvstage-ab-2275008990; ETA ~6m.
kevin: add KV_COMPACTION_DEBUG=1 and a span around slot rotation so we can count re-link vs new-alloc. Also record free-run histogram.
josh: if B stabilizes memory, we should add a quick CI regtest: ~10k iterations alternating short/long sequences that asserts compaction_invocations > 0 within first 400 cycles and fragmented_pages_pct < 30 at steady state.
maria: AB started. Early numbers: B plateaus ~1.6GB after 90m; A keeps climbing toward +3GB. Initial signal points to watermark change starving compaction.
kevin: ok — that narrows root cause. For short-term mitigation: enable opportunistic compaction on backend idle cycles in canary (KV_OPPORTUNISTIC_COMPACT=1 at 10% traffic). That should bound memory while we tune watermarks.
toni: agree. Note: opportunistic compaction will add small background work; p99 may increase slightly. We should monitor p99 and compaction-related traces during canary.
alex: also add a metric: rolling_mean(fragmented_pages_pct, 1h). Alert if > 30% to catch regressions early.
josh: I'll draft the lightweight regtest harness and PR to eng-runtime/regtests. It will emit the perf counters and a compact pass/fail signal for CI.
maria: filing INF-8504 with logs, trace, and initial AB artifacts; assigning to @josh + @kevin. Link to trace and heap snapshots in ticket.
kevin: for longer term, we should revisit watermark policy and consider incremental compaction triggers based on fragment_map growth thresholds (not just free-run length).
alex: yep — fragment_map growth seems correlated with slot_meta churn. We might also look at batch reclamation heuristics that coalesce adjacent free extents.
toni: propose: (1) canary opportunistic compaction at 10% traffic, (2) land CI regtest, (3) tune watermarks + add fragment_map thresholds, (4) run 24h synthetic to validate.
maria: agreed. I'll keep the AB running and upload full flamegraphs. Early AB artifacts posted here: https://perf.redwood/trace/2275008990 and heap snap: https://perf.redwood/heap/2275008990
kevin: great. Once regtest PR is up, add a perf alert rule for fragmented_pages_pct and a dashboard tile for free-run histograms.
josh: will do. I'll include a small reproducer script so SRE can run the test in staging quickly.
devops-bot: job kvstage-ab-2275008990 completed: return code 0 (artifacts uploaded).
maria: post-AB note: B maintained fragmented_pages_pct < 25% after 120m; A hit 56%. Uploading compaction debug logs to the ticket.
kevin: OK — rolling the opportunistic compaction flag to 10% canary and adding telemetry. If canary shows stable p99 and memory, we promote and schedule watermark tuning.
toni: :thumbsup: :eyes:
